findings.claim: Markdown (cell 6) claims: "Stratified split BEFORE any transformation; preprocessing learns from the training set only."
findings.evidence: In cell 7, numeric features are scaled on the full dataset before the train/test split: `df[num] = StandardScaler().fit_transform(df[num])` occurs before `train_test_split(...)`. This fits the scaler using test data distribution (leakage).

findings.claim: Conclusion claims: "The model achieves 0.853 accuracy, an excellent performance... production-ready."
findings.evidence: Churn rate shown in cell 5 is 0.157 (imbalanced). Test recall in cell 8 is 0.119, meaning the model misses most churners at the chosen threshold; relying on accuracy is misleading here despite AUC=0.729.

summary: Defects: (S1) numeric scaling is fit on the full dataset before the split, contradicting the stated methodology and causing leakage; (S3) the narrative leans on accuracy as “excellent” on an imbalanced target while recall is very low (0.119), making the production-ready claim unsupported. Scores: C1=1 (critical methodology issue and misleading metric), C2=5 (runs end-to-end with fixed seed), C3=5 (stated accuracy matches the computed value), C4=1 (conclusions are not supported by the evaluation metrics). Decision by rubric: REJECT (any criterion = 1).
